wars.cap: Thutmose I's campaign against Kerma: Egyptian victory; the kingdom of Kerma was defeated.

cs.c: N.M. Sherif (1981) Nubia before Napata (−3100 to −750), ch.9 (General History of Africa II)

bt.t: Tuthmose I conquered the northern Sudan, ending the independence of Kush.

s.c: N.M. Sherif (1981) Nubia before Napata (−3100 to −750), ch.9 (General History of Africa II)

bt.q: it was Tuthmose I ( — 1530 to —1520) who accomplished the conquest of the northern Sudan; thus bringing the independence of the kingdom of Kush to an end.

bt.t: Petronius, prefect of Roman Egypt, captured Napata; Rome garrisoned Primis (Qasr Ibrim).

bt.q: the prefect of Roman Egypt, Petronius, mounted a punitive expedition and captured Napata in —23. A permanent garrison was established by the Romans at Primis (Qasr Ibrim), which held off the Meroites.

bt.t: A permanent Roman garrison at Primis (Qasr Ibrim) held off the Meroites.

s.c: J. Leclant (1981) The empire of Kush: Napata and Meroe, ch.10 (General History of Africa II)

bt.q: A permanent garrison was established by the Romans at Primis (Qasr Ibrim), which held off the Meroites.

wars.cap: Ezana of Aksum reached the Atbara confluence and records an expedition 'against the Nubas'.

cs.c: J. Leclant (1981) The empire of Kush: Napata and Meroe, ch.10 (General History of Africa II)

bt.t: Ezana of Aksum reached the Atbara confluence and campaigned 'against the Nubas'.

s.c: J. Leclant (1981) The empire of Kush: Napata and Meroe, ch.10 (General History of Africa II)

bt.q: Ezana, the first monarch to embrace Christianity, reached the confluence of the Atbara and boasts of having mounted an expedition yielding much booty 'against the Nubas'.

wars.cap: An expedition from Egypt reached Dongola in 651–652; fierce Nubian resistance forced a truce.

cs.c: M. El Fasi and I. Hrbek (1988) Stages in the development of Islam and its dissemination in Africa, ch.3 (General History of Africa III)
T. Bianquis (1988) Egypt from the Arab conquest until the end of the Fatimid state (1171) (General History of Africa III, ch.7)

bt.t: An expedition from Egypt reached Dongola; fierce Nubian resistance forced a truce.

s.c: M. El Fasi and I. Hrbek (1988) Stages in the development of Islam and its dissemination in Africa, ch.3 (General History of Africa III)

bt.q: The Muslims from Egypt tried in 31/651-2 to conquer Nubia and even penetrated as far as Dongola but the fierce resistance of the Nubians forced them to seek a truce.

bt.t: 'Abd Allah b. Sa'd's expedition got as far as Dongola; the Christian population fiercely resisted.

s.c: T. Bianquis (1988) Egypt from the Arab conquest until the end of the Fatimid state (1171) (General History of Africa III, ch.7)

bt.q: In 31/652 'Abd Allah launched an expedition against Nubia, in present-day Sudan, and got as far as Dongola, upstream from the Third Cataract. The Christian population, close to the Monophysitic Church of Egypt, put up a fierce resistance.

wars.cap: Funj victory; the Abdallabi king became a Funj vassal.

cs.c: Y.F. Hasan and B.A. Ogot (1992) The Sudan, 1500–1800, ch.7 (General History of Africa V)

bt.t: At Arbaji the Funj defeated the 'Abdallab, whose king became a vassal.

s.c: Y.F. Hasan and B.A. Ogot (1992) The Sudan, 1500–1800, ch.7 (General History of Africa V)

bt.q: At Arbadji, in 1504, the Fundj defeated the 'Abdallabi and their king was reduced to the position of vassal.

wars.cap: Battle of Shaykan: Mahdist victory, a turning point of the Mahdist revolution.

cs.c: H.A. Ibrahim (based on a contribution by Abbas I. Ali) African initiatives and resistance in North-East Africa (General History of Africa VII, ch.4)

bt.q: Another turning-point in the history of the Mahdist revolution was the battle at Shaykān on 5 November 1883. … The Ansār completely annihilated their enemy at Shaykān's forest in the neighbourhood of al-'Obeid.

bt.t: Mahdist forces took Khartoum and killed Gordon, ending Turco-Egyptian rule.

s.c: H.A. Ibrahim (based on a contribution by Abbas I. Ali) African initiatives and resistance in North-East Africa (General History of Africa VII, ch.4)

bt.q: The emperor hastened to Matamma to resist them, but at the close of a victorious battle on 10 March 1889, was mortally wounded by a stray bullet. News of his death caused his army to disintegrate.

bt.q: Commanded by Emir Maḥmūd Aḥmad, the Ansār tried unsuccessfully to repel the enemy attack at the battle of Atbara on 8 April 1898.

s.c: H.A. Ibrahim (based on a contribution by Abbas I. Ali) African initiatives and resistance in North-East Africa (General History of Africa VII, ch.4)

bt.q: the Khalīfa decided to meet the enemy in the vicinity of his capital, Omdurman … the Sudanese fought the enemy with magnificent courage at the battle of Karari on 2 September 1898. Once again they were defeated by superior armaments.

wars.cap: The Torit mutiny of the Equatoria Corps, August 1955, is the start point of the first civil war.

bt.q: in August 1955 the Equatoria Corps of the Sudanese army revolted against the gradual take-over of the administration and command posts by the northerners. Although the mutineers soon surrendered, disorder had by that time spread through the southern provinces

J. Leclant (1981) The empire of Kush: Napata and Meroe, ch.10 (General History of Africa II)

wars.cap: Mamluk forces repeatedly installed rulers at Dongola and imposed tribute.

wars.cap: The Ottoman province of Berberistan, with garrisons at Ibrim, Aswan and Say.
